title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: Every SEC filing and cross-border deal has a zero-tolerance error budget; clients pay for software that automates the routine and experts who rescue the deadline.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: DFIN serves two core end-markets [1, 18]. The first is Capital Markets, which covers corporate issuers, investment banks, and M&A dealmakers. The second is Investment Companies, which serves mutual funds, exchange-traded funds, and alternative asset managers. Across both markets, DFIN delivers work through two distinct models: Software Solutions and Compliance & Communications Management (CCM) [1, 18]. This 2x2 grid creates four reporting segments that generated $767.0 million in FY2025 net sales [1, 15]. Capital Markets produced 68.6% of FY2025 revenue ($526.2 million), while Investment Companies added 31.4% ($240.8 million) [18]. Software Solutions reached $358.4 million in FY2025, or 46.7% of total sales, up 8.7% year-over-year [9, 10]. In Q3 2026, software crossed the halfway mark at 51.5% of revenue ($95.2 million out of $185.0 million) [11].

web_blocks.takeaway: Capital Markets represents 68.6% of total revenue and carries higher cyclicality, while Investment Companies (31.4%) provides steady, calendar-driven regulatory recurrence [15, 18].

web_blocks.html: Real customer workflows show how these four segments work in practice. In Capital Markets – Software Solutions (CM-SS, $230.0 million in FY2025), a newly public mid-cap biotech firm uses ActiveDisclosure for its Form 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K filings [18, 19]. Its controller links Excel trial balances directly into cloud tables. Legal counsel, external auditors, and the CFO can then edit footnotes at the same time without version conflicts [19, 20]. The team applies inline XBRL (iXBRL) tags and sends the validated filing straight to the SEC's EDGAR system [19, 20]. On the deal side, a private-equity sponsor selling an industrial business spins up a Venue Virtual Data Room [21, 22]. Rebuilt on a cloud-native stack in mid-2025, Venue hosts thousands of confidential contracts, runs AI-powered redaction and summaries, and tracks bidder diligence [21, 22]. ActiveDisclosure grew ~20% year-over-year in Q4 2025, ~29% in Q2 2026, and ~24% in Q3 2026, passing $100 million in trailing four-quarter revenue [10, 11, 23].

In Capital Markets – Compliance & Communications Management (CM-CCM, $296.2 million in FY2025), work shifts from self-serve SaaS to high-touch execution [18]. Imagine a Fortune 500 firm executing a complex spin-off or a contested proxy fight. Or picture a late-stage startup filing an S-1 with last-minute underwriter pricing changes at 2:00 a.m. Internal teams rarely manage those SEC formatting rules alone. DFIN's specialists step in to typeset, proof, convert exhibits, and manage EDGAR Next filing credentials [19, 24]. They also coordinate physical and digital delivery of prospectuses and proxy cards [19, 24]. CM-CCM earns lower gross margins than pure software and rises or falls with IPO and M&A deal counts. Even so, it serves as a vital funnel for ActiveDisclosure and Venue [23].

In Investment Companies – Software Solutions (IC-SS, $128.4 million in FY2025), a global asset manager with 150 mutual funds and ETFs uses DFIN's Arc Suite [18, 25, 26]. That suite includes ArcReporting, ArcPro, ArcRegulatory, and ArcDigital to automate recurring fund filings [18, 25, 26]. Under the SEC's Tailored Shareholder Reports (TSR) mandate, effective July 2024, funds can no longer rely on sprawling omnibus books [27, 28]. Instead, they must issue concise, visually structured, iXBRL-tagged annual and semi-annual reports for every share class [27, 28]. ArcReporting pulls portfolio holdings and performance feeds from fund accounting systems and fills standard templates [25, 27]. It then creates compliant iXBRL tags and publishes web versions via ArcDigital alongside Form N-PORT and Form N-CEN filings [25, 27].

In Investment Companies – Compliance & Communications Management (IC-CCM, $112.4 million in FY2025), that same asset manager relies on DFIN for physical delivery [18, 27]. DFIN prints, binds, and mails Tailored Shareholder Reports and summary prospectuses to retail investors who still want paper, while also offering managed composition [18, 27]. Because the TSR rule replaced multi-hundred-page books with 3–4 page summaries, print volumes and mailing revenue structurally shrank across 2024–2026 [27]. DFIN accepts this steady print runoff in IC-CCM while winning higher-margin, recurring Arc Suite software seats in IC-SS [9, 27].

web_blocks.title: The Hidden Cyclicality Inside Software Solutions
paragraphs: Investors should not treat all 'Software Solutions' revenue as pure recurring SaaS. Within CM-SS ($230.0M), ActiveDisclosure is mostly recurring subscription software. By contrast, Venue Virtual Data Rooms ($37.5M in Q2 2026) rely heavily on project and deal volume, rising and falling with M&A and capital-raising activity [23, 29].
Even ActiveDisclosure includes transactional non-subscription usage, such as S-1 IPO drafting. That transactional line surged ~69% year-over-year in Q2 2026 alongside a capital markets rebound [23].

web_blocks.title: Blind-Spot Patch: SEC Deregulatory Rule Reversals, E-Delivery Default & Geographic Mix
paragraphs: 1. SEC Deregulatory Agenda & E-Delivery Default Risk: Original underwriting treated SEC rules solely as a secular tailwind via Tailored Shareholder Reports (TSR) and EDGAR Next. However, under Chairman Paul Atkins, the SEC 2026 Regulatory Agenda (analyzed by K&L Gates in July 2026) introduces material rule-reversal and paper-runoff risks. In February 2026, the SEC proposed scaling back Form N-PORT portfolio reporting (an explicit ArcReporting workflow), while adding a cross-divisional rulemaking project to replace paper-by-default rules with an electronic-delivery default for fund and adviser disclosures alongside proxy cost-reduction amendments and expanded small-entity thresholds ($1B adviser / $10B fund AUM) (K&L Gates, July 8, 2026; SEC Chair Atkins remarks, April 21, 2026) [56]. An e-delivery default would directly accelerate shrinkage in DFIN's $109.4M TTM Print & Distribution line ($95.8M in 9M 2026) and $87.8M 9M 2026 IC-CCM revenue [45, 56].

2. Q3 2026 Segment Divergences & U.S. Geographic Concentration: In Q3 2026, consolidated net sales rose +5.5% YoY to $185.0M (CM-SS $64.1M +8.6%, CM-CCM $61.9M +8.2%, IC-SS $31.1M -1.9%, IC-CCM $27.9M +1.8%), and management guided Q4 2026 net sales to $175M-$180M with $50M in capital markets transactional revenue and 26%-27% Adjusted EBITDA margin (Q3 2026 Form 8-K EX-99.1) [45, 46]. Notably, FY2025 Form 10-K Note 16 confirms 89.3% U.S. revenue concentration ($684.8M of $767.0M), while Asia net sales contracted 32.5% from $36.6M in FY2023 to $24.7M in FY2025 amid subdued cross-border listings (FY2025 Form 10-K) [51].

book_paragraphs: To see how DFIN makes money, picture a four-quadrant grid. Across the top sit two customer worlds: Capital Markets and Investment Companies. Capital Markets serves public firms, investment banks, and private equity dealmakers. Investment Companies serves mutual funds, ETFs, and asset managers. Down the side sit two ways DFIN serves them: cloud Software Solutions and high-touch Compliance and Communications Management, or CCM.

Let's walk through all four quadrants with concrete examples. Start in Capital Markets Software Solutions, which brought in $230.0 million in 2025. Imagine a newly public biotech firm preparing its annual Form 10-K. Instead of emailing Word files back and forth with auditors at midnight, the controller works inside ActiveDisclosure. She links Excel tables to SEC filings, applies inline XBRL tags, and files straight to EDGAR. Now imagine a private-equity firm selling a factory unit. Its bankers open a Venue Virtual Data Room, upload thousands of contracts, use built-in AI to redact sensitive terms, and track buyer activity. ActiveDisclosure is recurring subscription software; Venue is transactional deal software.

Next, move to Capital Markets CCM, DFIN's largest segment at $296.2 million in 2025. When a company launches an IPO or fights a contested proxy battle, nobody wants a formatting error at 1:00 a.m. before a deadline. DFIN's compliance specialists act like air-traffic control. They typeset prospectuses, manage EDGAR Next permissions, and handle physical or digital shareholder mailings.

Now cross over to the Investment Companies side of the house. In Investment Companies Software Solutions—$128.4 million in 2025—a large asset manager running 150 ETFs and mutual funds uses DFIN's Arc Suite. When the SEC's Tailored Shareholder Reports rule took effect in July 2024, funds had to replace thick, unreadable annual books with crisp, tagged summaries for each share class. ArcReporting pulls fund accounting data automatically and formats those reports at scale.

Finally, in Investment Companies CCM—$112.4 million in 2025—DFIN prints and mails those short shareholder reports to retail investors who still prefer paper over digital delivery. Because those books shrank from hundreds of pages to just a few, paper revenue is naturally falling over time. DFIN's long-term bet is simple: trade low-margin paper pages for high-margin software seats.

Two regulatory and geographic realities missed in the earlier narrative also deserve attention as of late 2026. First, regulatory rules cut both ways: while TSR and EDGAR Next boosted software adoption, the SEC 2026 rulemaking agenda includes proposed amendments scaling back Form N-PORT reporting and a cross-divisional project to make electronic delivery the default for mutual fund and adviser disclosures—a policy shift that would accelerate the structural decline of DFIN's remaining $109.4 million trailing Print and Distribution business. Second, DFIN remains overwhelmingly domestic, generating 89.3% of its FY2025 revenue ($684.8 million) inside the United States while Asian capital-markets revenue shrank by nearly a third between 2023 and 2025.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Not All Software Dollars Are Equal
book_callouts.text: When you hear that software crossed 51.5% of DFIN's revenue in Q3 2026, remember to look under the hood. ActiveDisclosure and Arc Suite behave like sticky, recurring enterprise SaaS. Venue Virtual Data Rooms, while cloud-hosted and high-margin, still beat to the rhythm of M&A and IPO deal volume.
